newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines to provide passenger lists.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines to provide passenger lists.

text.p: Seven U.S. airlines have agreed to promptly provide the State Department with passenger lists for American planes in crashes overseas, the department said on Tuesday.
The agreement was one of the recommendations by a special White House commission formed after the July 17 explosion of a TWA Boeing 747 off New York, killing all 230 people aboard.
Families of those killed in the crashes have often complained of difficulty in finding out promptly if relatives or friends were on board downed planes.
Airlines have said they were reluctant to release lists quickly without confirming their accuracy.
The department said the agreement had no force of law, but the Transportation Department was writing it into a binding airline regulation.

Department spokesman Glyn Davies said in future accidents, when airlines provide the passenger lists to the department, "we, in turn, can perform our function of helping the families of victims to know precisely what has occurred to their loved ones."
The airlines signing the agreement were American Airlines, Continental Airlines, Delta Air Lines, Northwest Airlines, TWA, United Airlines and USAir, the department said.
